spec.summary: The print studio autosaves the card in progress and keeps a gallery, but the photo and video studios keep nothing: a reload, a closed tab, a crash or quitting the desktop app throws away a whole Reel edit or a batch of edited photos, and an hour of timeline work can't be put down and picked up tomorrow. As the video editor grows (tracks, keyframes, audio, and next voice-over, whose recordings exist nowhere else, 209), that loss gets worse. 408 makes photo batches and video projects **saved projects**: saved automatically as you work, listed so you can keep several, reopened exactly as you left them. Storage follows how each version of the app already stores the print gallery (docs/DESKTOP.md): the **browser** keeps projects and copies of their media in the browser's own storage on this device, because a web page can't open a file by its path again; the **desktop app** keeps projects as files in its data folder and remembers where each photo, video and sound file is on disk instead of copying it, because desktop videos can be 50 GB. The two libraries stay separate, as the print galleries are today. Nothing is uploaded.

US-1.text: As a creator editing a Reel, I want my work saved as I go, so that a reload, a crash or closing the app never loses it.

US-2.text: As a creator, I want to keep several projects (this week's Reel, a YouTube video, a photo carousel) and switch between them, so that I can work on more than one thing.

US-3.text: As a browser user, I want a reopened project to have its photos, videos and sounds without picking the files again, and to know how much space my projects take on this device.

US-4.text: As a desktop user with large video files, I want projects to point to my files where they are instead of copying gigabytes, and to be helped to find a file I moved.

US-5.text: As a creator, I want to delete a project and get its space back, without the app ever deleting my own original files.

US-6.text: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want to create, open, rename and delete projects without a mouse and hear what happened.

AC-1.text: **Autosave**: the video project and the photo batch are saved within 2 s of the last change (a drag or slider saves once it ends), and at once when the tab is hidden, the window closes or the app quits. There is no Save button to forget; the top bar shows “Saved” / “Saving…” / “Not saved: <reason>”. A crash or power cut loses at most the last 2 s of edits, and a project is never left half-written: after an interrupted save the project opens as it was at the last complete save.

AC-2.text: **Everything comes back**: reopening a project (after a reload, in a new tab, after restarting the app or the computer) restores every saved setting: for video the format, tracks, clips, gaps, layers, keyframes, transitions, speed and ramps, audio tracks, sound clips, ducking, loudness, export settings and the playhead; for photos every photo, its order, edits, masks, layers, the post format and export settings. For the fixture projects of 201–208 and of the photo editor, the reopened project's saved document is identical to the one saved, and its export is byte-identical to the export before reopening. The undo history starts empty (Q2).

AC-3.text: **Several projects**: each studio (photo, video) has a **Projects** list (Q6): **New**, **Open**, **Rename**, **Duplicate** and **Delete** (asks first). Each entry shows its name, a thumbnail, its kind (Reel / Short / YouTube / photo post), its length or photo count, when it was last changed and the space it takes on this device; newest first. A new project is named after its kind and time (“Reel · 19 Oct 14:02”) and can be renamed (1–80 characters). Opening the studio reopens the last project used; the first visit starts a new one. There is no limit on the number of projects other than the device's storage.

AC-4.text: **Browser storage**: every photo, video and sound a project uses is copied once into the browser's storage on this device when it is added (Q3), so a reopened project needs no file to be picked again. A file used by several projects, or added twice, is stored once. Copying runs in the background with progress and never blocks editing; until it finishes the project says the file isn't kept yet. The app asks the browser to keep its storage (persistent storage, so it isn't cleared to free space) and, if the browser refuses, says that projects may be removed when the device runs low. A file that wouldn't fit in the space the browser allows is refused with the reason and the space left (“This 2.1 GB video doesn't fit: 1.4 GB left for projects in this browser”).

AC-5.text: **Desktop storage**: projects are files in the app's data folder (`library/projects/`). Photo, video and sound files the user added are **not copied**: the project remembers each one's location, size and modification time (Q4). Files the app itself made and that exist nowhere else (209's voice recordings, generated music, AI images, Pexels downloads, pasted images) are kept in the data folder (`library/media/`). Opening a project whose file was moved, renamed, changed or deleted still opens: the missing clip shows a placeholder with **Find file…**; choosing the file reconnects it (refused with the reason when it isn't the same kind of media or is shorter than the clip needs), and other missing files of the project found in the same folder reconnect at once.

AC-6.text: **Loading is validated**: every project read from storage goes through the existing validators (the project document's and the photo edits'): a damaged project, one from a newer version of the app, or one with values out of range opens with everything that is valid, clamped where needed, and says what was left out; it never crashes the studio or loses the rest of the list. A project that can't be read at all stays in the list marked “can't be opened” with **Delete**, and its media is kept until it is deleted.

AC-7.text: **Deleting gives the space back, and never touches the user's files**: deleting a project removes it and any stored media no other project uses (the browser's copies; on desktop only the app-made files in `library/media/`). A user's own files on disk are never deleted, moved or changed by the app. The list shows the space a delete will free before asking.

AC-8.text: **One project, one editor at a time** (Q15): opening a project already open in another tab or window takes it over there: the other one stops saving at once and says “This project is open in another window” with **Open here again**. Two windows never overwrite each other's edits silently.

AC-9.text: **Space on the device**: the Projects list shows the total used and, in the browser, the space the browser allows (“Projects use 3.2 GB; about 41 GB free for this site”). At 90 % of the allowed space it warns once per session; when a save fails because storage is full, the project stays open in memory, the top bar says “Not saved: storage is full”, and saving resumes once space is freed. The print studio's gallery, photo store and autosave are unchanged and share nothing with projects (Q8).

AC-10.text: **Saving and opening don't slow editing**: saving a 500-clip video project or a 20-photo batch blocks the page for under 50 ms on the reference laptop; opening a 60-clip project shows its timeline within 2 s (thumbnails, filmstrips and waveforms may fill in after, from what was saved, Q14) and plays within 3 s; the entry chunk stays ≤ 350 KB (the projects code loads with `import()`). (Measured in 290.)

AC-11.text: The Projects list and every action in it work from the keyboard (arrow keys move, Enter opens, F2 renames, Delete asks to delete) and are announced (“Opened Reel · 19 Oct 14:02, 24 clips”, “Deleted Holiday carousel, 210 MB freed”); the save status is a polite live region announced only on a failure; axe finds no violations with the list open. (Proven in 290.)

AC-12.text: End to end in the browser (desktop and phone layouts): make a Reel with a video, a photo, text and a sound, reload, and it is all back and exports the same file; delete it and the browser's stored size goes back to what it was. In the desktop app on Windows and macOS: the same after quitting and restarting; a moved file reconnects with Find file…. (Proven in 290.)

AC-13.text: **Agent tools** (Constitution XI, Q10): `list_projects`, `new_project`, `open_project`, `rename_project` and `delete_project` for both studios, going through the same code as the UI; a deleted project needs `confirm: true`. Covered by the self-test and `test:mcp`, documented in `docs/MCP.md`. (Run in 290.)

AC-14.text: `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (projects, autosave, storage, Find file…), `docs/DESKTOP.md` (the `projects/` and `media/` folders, the separate libraries), `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` (storage full, a project that can't be opened, browser storage cleared), `specs/architecture.md` §6 (the storage table), `specs/lld.md`, `docs/MCP.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the in-app docs describe the change.

Q1.text: One autosaved project per studio, or a list? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ a list (AC-3): creators run several Reels at once, and a single autosave slot would make **New** throw the old one away. The last one used reopens, so for someone with one project it feels like a single autosave.

Q2.text: Save the undo history? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ no: it starts empty when a project is reopened. Saving it would multiply what is written on every change, and the print studio doesn't either.

Q3.text: How does the browser keep media? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ copy each file into the browser's own storage for this site (AC-4), in every browser. The alternative, keeping a handle to the original file (Chrome and Edge only), needs the user to grant access again on every visit and fails when the file moves, so it isn't used. The cost is space, so files are stored once however many projects use them, and the size is shown.

Q4.text: How does the desktop app keep media? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ remember where the user's files are and never copy them (AC-5): desktop videos can be up to 50 GB and copying would double the disk used. Files only the app has (recordings, generated or downloaded media) go into the data folder, so nothing exists only in memory. A **Copy files into the project** option (for moving to another computer) is left for project files (Q7).

Q5.text: How large can the browser's projects get? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ as large as the browser allows for the site (Chrome allows up to 60 % of the disk, Firefox up to 50 % of free space, Safari asks past ~1 GB), with the space shown and a clear refusal when a file wouldn't fit; no limit of our own. The existing per-file limits (4 GB video on the web) stay.

Q6.text: Where is the Projects list? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ a **Projects** button at the left of each studio's top bar (next to the mark) opening a panel with the list and New; plus a **Continue: <project>** link on the home screen when there is a recent project. No separate screen.

Q7.text: Project files (`.chitthi` for a video or photo project, with or without its media) to move a project between computers or between the browser and the desktop app? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ not in 408: it needs packing gigabytes of media into one file and streaming it, which is its own feature (a follow-up, 409). 209's AC-8 drops its `.chitthi` clause until then.

Q8.text: Do projects share anything with the print studio? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ no: the print gallery, photo store and card autosave stay as they are (AC-9). A photo used in a print card and in a photo project is stored for each, as today.

Q9.text: What is a photo project? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ the photo studio's batch (up to the batch limit), with its format, edits and export settings: each saved batch is a project. RAW files are kept as the original file (browser: copied; desktop: referenced) so they can be developed again.

Q10.text: Agent tools? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ yes, the five of AC-13, because every user-facing feature must be reachable by agents (Constitution XI) and agents already build Reels and photo posts through the MCP server.

Q11.text: When are 408's e2e, self-test and timing checks run? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ in 290, the Phase 2 test pass, with Phase 2's (D-033), and 408 ships in the 3.0.0 release with Phase 2, since 209 depends on it.

Q12.text: How do 209's voice recordings relate? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ a recording is project media made by the app: in the browser stored like any copied file, on desktop in `library/media/`; 209's own take store then keeps only takes in progress, for crash recovery (D-058).

Q13.text: How quickly is a change saved? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ within 2 s of the last change, and at once when the tab is hidden or the window closes (AC-1); the document is written whole each time (it is small: media is stored separately), media only when added.

Q14.text: Are thumbnails, filmstrips and waveform peaks saved? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ yes, with the project (small: tens of KB to a few MB), so a reopened project looks complete at once instead of re-reading every file; they are rebuilt in the background if missing or if the file changed.

Q15.text: Two tabs or windows on the same project? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-19):_ the latest one opened takes over and the other stops saving and says so (AC-8), on the web across tabs and on desktop across windows. Merging edits from two windows is out of scope.

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- **Reliability:** at most 2 s of edits lost to a crash; never a half-written project; a damaged project never takes the others down (AC-1, AC-6).
- **Performance:** saving blocks the page < 50 ms; media copying and loading run in the background; the projects code loads with `import()`, entry chunk ≤ 350 KB (AC-10).
- **Privacy:** everything stays on the device; nothing is uploaded (Constitution VI). Desktop keeps file locations only in its own data folder.
- **Security (desktop):** reading the user's files by location goes through validated IPC registered with `electron/ipc.cjs`, only for files the user added to a project or chose with Find file…; the page never gets arbitrary file access.
- **Compatibility:** browser and desktop alike in behaviour, each with its own storage (AC-4, AC-5); Chromium, Firefox and Safari; existing print data untouched; projects made by this version open in later ones (versioned documents through the validators).
- **Accessibility:** keyboard and screen reader for every action; axe passes (AC-11).
- **Free and open source:** no limit on projects other than the device's space; no account or cloud.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- Project files for moving or sharing a project, with or without media (Q7, follow-up 409); copying a desktop project's files into one folder.
- Sync between devices, between the browser and the desktop app, or any cloud storage.
- Saving the undo history (Q2); version history or snapshots of a project.
- Merging edits made in two windows (Q15).
- Changes to the print studio's gallery, photo store or autosave (Q8).

risks.text: **R1 Desktop media through `chitthi-media://`** (D1): `<video>` seeking, Mediabunny `UrlSource` range reads in the page and the scan worker, the decode pool's speed compared with a `File`, and the CSP. Mitigation: spike task first: a 4 GB local video through the scheme plays, seeks, scans, exports at the speed of today's `File` path (within 10 %); if `UrlSource` is too slow, a `StreamSource` reading ranges over IPC instead.

**R2 OPFS across browsers** (Safari's missing main-thread `createWritable`, Firefox quotas, private windows without OPFS). Mitigation: the spike also copies a 1 GB file in Chrome, Firefox and Safari; the worker path for Safari; where OPFS is missing (private windows), projects save without media and say “files aren't kept in a private window”.

**R3 Touching every decode site** (§5) risks regressions in 204–208. Mitigation: one helper (`mediaInput`) and a mechanical change per site, done in one task before anything else; the existing unit tests and 290's self-test cover the paths; `MediaFile` is a Blob on the web, so the web path is unchanged in behaviour.
**R4 Quota surprises**: the browser may evict non-persisted storage. Mitigation: `persist()` asked and shown (AC-4); the cache and documents are small; TROUBLESHOOTING explains it.

**R5 Saving on close**: `pagehide` gives no time for async work in some browsers. Mitigation: saves are already at most 2 s old; the desktop app waits for `flush()` before closing (bounded at 2 s); the 2 s loss bound of AC-1 holds without the close save.

**R6 Security of the new IPC and scheme** (Constitution IX). Mitigation: paths never come from the page; ids validated; the scheme answers only indexed ids with matching size and mtime; unit tests for refusal cases (AC-5); reviewed against `specs/architecture.md` §7 in the docs task.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
Half the work exists: the video project already has a JSON shape (`engine/projectDoc.ts`, `toDocument`) and one validator (`engine/projectGate.ts`, `mergeProject`), and the photo edits and layers have theirs (`mergeEdit`, `mergeLayers`). Nothing writes or reads them: `VState` and `IgState` live in memory, each clip, sound and photo holding a `Blob` from the file picker. 408 adds (a) the conversions between the stores and the documents, (b) one **project library** interface with two implementations, browser and desktop, chosen once in `lib/` as `lib/db.ts` already does for the print gallery, (c) a **media store** behind the same split, (d) autosave and the Projects panel. Under D-033 every task is proven by unit tests (pure conversions and gates, the library against an in-memory implementation, the Electron handlers in `tests/unit/electron`); e2e, self-test and timing go to 290.

**§1 Documents (`engine/projectDoc.ts`, new `engine/photoProjectDoc.ts`, AC-2, AC-6).** `videoDocument(state)` builds a `ProjectDoc` from `VState` (each `VClip` / `VSound` → `DocClip` / `DocAudio` with a media id, `DocMedia` for each file) plus the fields the document lacks today: `name`, `playhead`, `trackView`; `videoFromDocument(doc, media)` is the reverse, after `mergeProject`. The photo batch gets the same pair: `PhotoProjectDoc { version: 1, name, format, limit, fileType, quality, caption, selected, items: { id, name, media, w, h, edit, layers, raw? }[], media: DocMedia[] }` and `mergePhotoProject(raw)` (each item through `mergeEdit` and `mergeLayers`, unknown or newer versions handled as `mergeProject` does: what's valid opens, reasons listed). Both are pure, so AC-2's round trip (document → store → document identical; 201–208 fixtures) is a unit test.

**§2 Media ids and fingerprints (`engine/mediaKey.ts`, AC-4).** A file's media id is its fingerprint: size + type + an FNV-1a hash of its first and last 64 KB (as `lib/photoKey.ts` does for data URLs), read with `Blob.slice` so a 4 GB file costs 128 KB of reading. The same file added twice or in two projects has one id and is stored once. A collision would need the same size, type and 128 KB of ends; D3 offers a full hash instead.

**§3 The project library (`lib/projects.ts`, `lib/projectsWeb.ts`, `lib/projectsDesktop.ts`, AC-3, AC-7, AC-9).** One interface, `ProjectLibrary`: `list()` (entries: id, studio, name, kind, length or photo count, changed, bytes, thumbnail, readable), `read(id)`, `write(id, doc, entry)`, `writeCache(id, cache)`, `readCache(id)`, `remove(id)` (removes media no other project uses and returns the bytes freed), `usage()`. `lib/projectLibrary.ts` exports `projects = desktop ? desktopProjects(desktop.projects) : webProjects()` (its own module: the implementations import the shared helpers of `lib/projects.ts`), and an in-memory implementation used by every unit test. The **cache** is what's slow to rebuild and small: clip thumbnails, filmstrips, photo preview JPEGs, waveform peaks (Q14), written only when it changes.
- **Browser (`projectsWeb.ts`):** IndexedDB database `chitthi-projects` (its own, so the print `chitthi` database's version doesn't move, D5) with stores `entries`, `docs`, `cache`; each write is one transaction, so a save is all or nothing (AC-1).
- **Desktop (`projectsDesktop.ts` → IPC → `electron/projects.cjs`):** `library/projects/<id>.json` (the document), `<id>.entry.json`, `<id>.cache.json`, each written to `<name>.tmp` and renamed over the old one, so an interrupted save leaves the last complete file (AC-1).

**§4 The media store (`lib/mediaStore.ts`, `lib/mediaWeb.ts`, `lib/mediaDesktop.ts`, AC-4, AC-5, AC-7).** `MediaStore`: `keep(file, owned)` (returns the media id; runs in the background with progress), `open(id)` (a `MediaFile` to play and decode, or `missing`), `relink(id)`, `sweep(usedIds)`, `usage()`.
- **Browser (`mediaWeb.ts`, D2):** each file is copied into the Origin Private File System, `media/<id>`, streamed (`file.stream()` into a writable, in a worker with a sync access handle where the main-thread writable is missing, Safari), so a 4 GB video never sits in memory. Reopened, `getFile()` gives a disk-backed `File`: the existing Blob code (Mediabunny's `BlobSource`, `<video>` from an object URL) works unchanged. Before copying, `navigator.storage.estimate()` is checked and a file that doesn't fit is refused with the space left (AC-4); `navigator.storage.persist()` is asked once, and its answer shown (AC-4).
- **Desktop (`mediaDesktop.ts` → IPC → `electron/media.cjs`, D1):** a file the user added isn't copied. The preload turns the picked `File` into its path (`webUtils.getPathForFile`, so the page can only name files the user actually picked or dropped), and the main process records `id → { path, size, mtime }` in `library/media-index.json`, which **only the main process writes**; the page refers to media by id only, never by path. App-made files (209's recordings, generated music, AI images, Pexels downloads, pasted images: `keep(file, true)`) are written into `library/media/<id>` through the existing chunked write pattern. Playing and decoding go through a privileged scheme `chitthi-media://<id>` served by the main process with `Range` support from the indexed path; it answers only for ids in the index whose file still has the recorded size and mtime (else 404, and the clip is missing). **Find file…** is a main-process open dialog: the chosen file is checked (kind, length via the page after it plays) and replaces the index entry; other missing ids whose file name exists in the chosen folder are reconnected at once (AC-5).

**§5 Media in the stores (`engine/mediaFile.ts`, the decode sites, AC-2, AC-5).** `VClip.file`, `VSound.file` and `IgItem.file` become `MediaFile = Blob | DiskMedia` (`DiskMedia { id, url, size, type, name }`, desktop only). One helper, `mediaInput(file)`, returns Mediabunny's `BlobSource` for a Blob and its `UrlSource` (range requests) for disk media; the 14 decode sites (`frameSource`, `decodePool`, `poolLane`, `exportSound`, `soundScan.worker`, `videoExport`, `instagramExport`, previews …) call it instead of `new BlobSource(file)`. `<video>` / `<audio>` already play `url` (an object URL today, `chitthi-media://` for disk media). Photos are small: `blobOf(file)` fetches disk media once into a Blob for `createImageBitmap`. A missing file (`missing: true`) draws a hatched placeholder with its name in the preview, and the export is refused with “Find the missing files first: …” (D4).

**§6 Autosave (`state/projectSave.ts`, AC-1, AC-9).** Subscribes to both stores; a change that alters the document (not the playhead during play, selections or view state; `trackView` and the playhead are written with the next real save or on hide) schedules a save 2 s after the last one, and `visibilitychange` → hidden, `pagehide` and the desktop window's close (`before-quit` waits for a `flush()` over IPC, at most 2 s) save at once. Saving serialises with `videoDocument` / photo document and `JSON.stringify` (under 50 ms for 500 clips, measured in 290, AC-10) and calls `projects.write`. Status for the top bar: `saved | saving | failed(reason)`; a failure (quota, disk full) keeps the project in memory, says “Not saved: …”, logs with `logError('handled', …)` and retries on the next change or every 30 s (AC-9). Media is kept (§4) when it is added, before the save that references it.

**§7 Opening, new, current project (`state/projects.ts`, AC-3).** `openProject(id)`: read, gate (`mergeProject` / `mergePhotoProject`), `media.open` each id, then `loadVideoProject` (extended with the settings it doesn't take today: format, fps, quality, kind, fadeOut, playhead, name) or the photo equivalent, rebuilding previews from the cache or the file. The route follows the project's kind (a YouTube project opens `#/instagram/youtube`, D6). `newProject(studio, kind)` names it “Reel · 19 Oct 14:02”. The last project per studio is remembered in `localStorage` (`chitthi-projects-last`); opening a studio reopens it, else starts a new one. Rename (1–80 characters), duplicate (the document and cache copied; media shared by id) and delete (AC-7) go through the library.

**§8 One editor at a time (`lib/projectLock.ts`, AC-8).** A `BroadcastChannel('chitthi-projects')`: opening a project posts `{ open: id, by }`; a tab or window holding that id stops saving at once, shows “This project is open in another window” with **Open here again** (which posts the same and reloads the project from storage). Works across browser tabs and across Electron windows (same origin).

**§9 The UI (`components/studio/ProjectsPanel.tsx`, `Shell.tsx`, home, AC-3, AC-9, AC-11).** A **Projects** button at the left of the studio top bar (both studios, Q6) opens a lazy-loaded panel: New (with the kind for video), the list (thumbnail, name, kind, length or photos, changed, size; newest first), Open, Rename (F2), Duplicate, Delete (asks, showing the space freed), storage used and allowed, the persistent-storage note, and “can't be opened” entries with Delete only (AC-6). Arrow keys move, Enter opens; actions are announced. The top bar shows the save status (a polite live region that speaks only on failure). The home screen gets **Continue: <name>** for the most recent project. Missing files list with **Find file…** in the clip's inspector and in a bar over the timeline (desktop).

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **Storage split chosen once** (as `lib/db.ts`): `desktop ? desktopX(desktop.x) : webX`. Callers never branch on the platform.
- **Browser media in OPFS** (`navigator.storage.getDirectory()`), streamed: `file.stream().pipeTo(handle.createWritable())`, or in a worker with `createSyncAccessHandle` where `createWritable` is missing (Safari). The `File` from `getFile()` is disk-backed, so reopened media behaves like a picked file. Quota from `navigator.storage.estimate()`, `persist()` asked once.
- **Desktop media by reference**, secured by keeping paths out of the page: the preload's `webUtils.getPathForFile` only works on real picked or dropped files; the main process writes `media-index.json`; the page only ever sees ids and `chitthi-media://<id>` URLs. The scheme is registered privileged (`stream`, `supportFetchAPI`, `secure`, `corsEnabled`, `bypassCSP: false`) and served with `Range` / `206` from `fs.createReadStream(start, end)`, checking size and mtime first. Mediabunny's `UrlSource` reads it with range requests in the page and in the scan worker.
- **Atomic writes**: desktop `tmp` + `rename` (same folder, so same volume); browser one IndexedDB transaction per save.
- **Autosave** is a debounce on the document-changing actions (the stores already know undo steps: `change()` / `commit()`), plus immediate saves on `visibilitychange` / `pagehide` and an IPC `flush` before the desktop window closes.
- **Reference counting by sweep**: after a delete, the media ids still used are collected from every project's document, and the rest is deleted (browser copies; desktop only app-made files and index entries, never the user's files). No counters to drift.
- **No new dependency.** Mediabunny (MPL-2.0, already shipped) has `UrlSource`; everything else is the platform.

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer (accepted 2026-10-19: D1–D6 as recommended)
sections.markdown:
**D1 How the desktop app plays and decodes files it only references.** **Recommended:** a privileged `chitthi-media://<id>` scheme served by the main process with Range support, read by `<video>` / `<audio>` and by Mediabunny's `UrlSource`; paths stay in the main process. Alternative: a `StreamSource` reading byte ranges over IPC (no scheme, but every decode read crosses IPC and `<video>` still needs a URL). The spike (R1) confirms the speed.

**D2 How the browser keeps media.** **Recommended:** the Origin Private File System (disk-backed `File`s, streamed copies, no size cap of its own). Alternative: Blobs in IndexedDB (simpler, but large Blobs are slower and some browsers buffer them in memory on write).

**D3 Media ids.** **Recommended:** a fingerprint of size, type and the first and last 64 KB (fast for 4 GB files). Alternative: a full SHA-256 (no collision risk, but hashing a 4 GB file takes ~10–20 s).

**D4 Exporting with missing files.** **Recommended:** refused with the list of missing files until they are found or their clips removed. Alternative: export with black frames and silence in their place.

**D5 The browser database.** **Recommended:** a new database `chitthi-projects`, so the print `chitthi` database's version and upgrade code don't change. Alternative: new stores in `chitthi` (version 6).

**D6 One video list for all kinds.** **Recommended:** the video studio's list holds Reels, Shorts and YouTube projects together (with their kind shown); opening one switches the studio to its mode. Alternative: a list per mode.
